land.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

successors.note: The Haudenosaunee took Huronia in 1649 (Iroquois page: 'defeated and assimilated most of the Huron (1649)'). The survivors fled to Gahoendoe (Christian Island), then to Quebec and the upper Great Lakes, and joined the Petun as the Wyandot; the pages call this a dispersal, with the Wendat Confederacy 're-established' in 1999, not a continuing territory.

capitals.name: Huronia (Ossossane, Quienonascaran)
capitals.note: The page names the capitals as 'Ossossane (during Brebeuf and the Jesuits), Quienonascaran (during Sagard), and possibly Carhagouha (in 1615)' without coordinates or years; the dot is the middle of the homeland between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe.

correction.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1450-1648 (Cliopatria has no Wendat row). 'Their original homeland extended to the Georgian Bay of Lake Huron and Lake Simcoe in Ontario'; the page gives no area (the village sizes only, 'one to ten acres'), a population of 20,000 to 40,000 at contact and 'about 12,000' after the 1634-1640 epidemics. The discs of 45 and 40 km round Orillia and Barrie cover about 8,500 km2 (the two discs overlap), the researcher's reading, to be replaced by a Huronia region when the gazetteer has one.

ledger.note: 15th century: the Wendat confederacy forms between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe. The page gives no year: 'The Wendat first emerged as a confederacy of five nations'; 'The Attinniaoenten and Hatingeennonniahak allied in the 15th century'. 1450 is the researcher's midpoint for the 15th century (page silent on the year).

ledger.note: 16 March 1649: the Haudenosaunee enter Wendake. 'a Haudenosaunee war party of about 1,000 entered Wendake and burned the Huron mission villages', killing about 300.

region.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1649: Wendake is abandoned. 'By May 1, 1649 the Huron had burned 15 of their villages' to keep stores from the Iroquois and fled; about 10,000 'fled to Gahoendoe (now also called Christian Island)', where 'most ... starved over the winter'; the Wyandot page: Wendake 'was destroyed by the Haudenosaunee in 1649' and about half the villages lost.

ledger.note: 1649: the fighting for Wendake ends with the homeland empty; the Iroquois page: the League 'defeated and assimilated most of the Huron (1649)'.

region.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

ledger.note: 1649: the Wendat Confederacy loses its homeland. The survivors scatter: some to Quebec ('resettled near Quebec City at Wendake'), others 'took refuge with the Petun' and moved west to Michilimackinac (1671) and Detroit (1701) as the Wyandot; the page says the confederacy was 'defeated and dispersed during the Beaver Wars' and 'reaffirmed in 1999'.

wars.name: Beaver Wars (Wendat campaign)

zones.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

wars.outcome: The Haudenosaunee destroyed Wendake in 1649; about 10,000 Wendat fled to Christian Island, where most starved, and the survivors dispersed to Quebec, the Petun and the upper Great Lakes.
wars.note: The Wyandot page: firearms-equipped Haudenosaunee raids from 1647. The Beaver Wars page: a 'devastating attack' in the winter of 1648. The Huron page: the war party of 16 March 1649, and 15 villages burned by 1 May. Epidemics in 1634-1640 had cut the Wendat from over 30,000 to about 12,000 beforehand.

certainty.note: The homeland is known by the villages' archaeology and by the pages' 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe'; no frontier is given.

notes: New state (Cliopatria has no Wendat row). Page budget 2-5: three pages (Huron people, Wyandot people, Beaver Wars); Wendat_Confederacy and Wendake_(historical_region) did not load (URL not found) and Huronia is a disambiguation page. The 'Huron people' page gives no area, so the single keyframe is two discs round Orillia and Barrie, the gazetteer lacking a Huronia region (gazetteer name needed: region 'Huronia' / 'Wendake', Simcoe County and the Georgian Bay shore, Ontario). Start 1450 is a midpoint of 'the 15th century' (page silent); a gap-filler should open the archaeology of the Huron (Draper, Mantle sites). The mirror events are in haudenosaunee: contest 1648-1649 and the gain of Huronia in 1649. Disagreements: the first Haudenosaunee raids 1647 (Wyandot) or the devastating attack of 1648 (Beaver Wars) or the destruction of 1649 (Huron and Wyandot pages). The Petun (Tionontati), whom survivors joined, and the Wyandot of Michilimackinac and Detroit need their own dossier if the project wants them (counterparts_needing_dossiers: Petun). Gazetteer: no names beyond Orillia and Barrie.
